content.summary: The literal theorem, maximum-size convention, arbitrary-support scope, hereditary size-68 reduction, and stated distinction between imported theorems and local computational evidence withstand this Round 1 adversarial framing review. One notation and quantifier clarification is required for the neighbourhood upper bounds used by the graph reductions. This is not acceptance of the finite exclusions, which were not replayed or fully audited in this round.
required_revisions: Define the scalar N used in Sections 5.1 and 6, explicitly state whether each N<=c means |N[R]|<=c for every actual member R, and define an N43 anchor as an actual R with |N[R]|=43. This makes the quantifier needed for minimum disjointness-graph degree explicit.

findings.statement: Section 3 defines the set N[R] and the minimum mu, but Sections 5.1 and 6 subsequently use an undefined scalar N in N<=46,45,44,43 and the phrase N43 anchor. The inference to a graph minimum-degree bound requires a universal upper bound on |N[R]|, not an upper bound for just one anchor or for the minimum.
findings.disposition: Add the missing scalar definition and explicit quantifier; the companion composition appears to intend the required universal bound.

findings.statement: The manuscript treats H27 and the pinned prior classifications as mathematical imports and discloses that the full external H27 ledger and all 42 prior suites were not replayed. The claim is therefore an ordinary computer-assisted theorem using cited results, not an end-to-end locally reconstructed or Lean-certified theorem.
findings.disposition: The framing is appropriately qualified in Sections 2 and 7; preserve these limitations in later versions.

checks.scope: Frozen Round 1 integrity and reviewer assignment
checks.method: Computed SHA-256 of manuscript bytes and canonical sorted compact JSON for snapshot, contract and roster using Python standard-library hashlib/json; read the exact alpha roster entry.
checks.observation: The manuscript hash is 2c200bf5dff9e665e7dab3ba3f5a1ef019251d341a1913d1f5bd2fc3c086f937 and canonical snapshot hash is 7912a1f1de1f27d72b2a2e660626f338303bf8cf71085720b4c1e304e670b5ba, both matching the assignment. Contract and roster canonical hashes match snapshot commitments. The five inspected global-proof/global-dag/external-scope/prior-ledger/prior-unlock files also match their evidence hashes.

checks.scope: Literal theorem and passage from at least 68 members to exactly 68
checks.method: Read manuscript Sections 1 and 4 and GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md, Literal statement and Mathematical proof by maximum degree; independently checked hereditary properties.
checks.observation: Restricting to any 68 distinct members preserves exact four-uniformity and absence of every three-sunflower, including the empty core. Thus excluding cardinality 68 gives maximum size at most 67, with no forcing-threshold shift. Complete-star retention is separately mentioned for branches that require it; no minimum positive degree is inherited through arbitrary deletion.

checks.scope: Initial neighbourhood lower bound and graph translation
checks.method: Checked the elementary implication directly against manuscript Section 3, EXTERNAL-H27-JIN-SCOPE.md, and pinned repository/paper/main.tex lines 132-165.
checks.observation: For actual R, two disjoint members of D(R) would form an empty-core sunflower with R, so D(R) is intersecting and H27 gives |N[R]|>=68-27=41. Independent sets of the disjointness graph are intersecting subfamilies, so alpha(G)<=27. The closed neighbourhood convention correctly gives deg_G(R)=68-|N[R]|.

checks.scope: Guard activation and use of the prior size-69 paper
checks.method: Read manuscript Sections 2-4, PRIOR_DELTA18_UNLOCK.md, global roadmap, and pinned source main.tex lines 333-350, 612-636 and 968-1024.
checks.observation: The triple cap 20 and complete high-link decompositions occur before the prior size-69 reduction. The crowding and cross-star results explicitly require mu>=41 and Delta<=18, and cross-star centres must avoid both tail supports. The proposed global order activates these guarded imports only after degree 20 and 19 are excluded; it does not cite the old upper 68 as a premise. This checks declared architecture, not every model row.

checks.scope: Neighbourhood upper-bound notation needed by low-degree graph arguments
checks.method: Read all manuscript definitions and the occurrences of N in Sections 5.1 and 6; compared with the graph identity deg_G(R)=68-|N[R]|.
checks.observation: N[R] and mu are defined, but a scalar N is not. The manuscript subsequently writes N<=44 and N<=43 and concludes graph minimum degrees 24 and 25. These implications are valid if N=max_R |N[R]|, which needs to be stated explicitly.

checks.scope: Scope of the present acceptance and computational assurance
checks.method: Compared the contract and manuscript Sections 3.1, 3.2 and 7 with the global source and foundation ledger.
checks.observation: The manuscript distinguishes shared-builder coefficient replay from separate literal coverage and separate low-degree reconstructions, and does not claim independent human certification or an assembled Lean theorem. All degree alternatives are enumerated at the architectural level, but this round has not verified the actual finite leaves or all arbitrary-support bridges.
